cluster.headline: Delhi civic body demolishes buildings after fatal Satya Niketan PG collapse
cluster.summary: After the September 6 building collapse in Delhi's Satya Niketan that killed seven people, the MCD inspected some 1,100 hostels and razed 24 buildings, including a girls' PG. Students are leaving the area, which grew from a resettlement colony into a student hub with buildings up to five storeys.

story.headline: MCD razes 24 buildings after fatal Satya Niketan PG collapse, Hindi outlets report
story.body:
Delhi's municipal corporation has demolished 24 buildings and inspected around 1,100 hostels in the Satya Niketan area following a building collapse that killed seven people, according to reporting by News18 Hindi. The outlet said a girls' paying-guest accommodation was among the structures brought down.

The intake note dates the collapse to September 6. The number of dead is given as seven in the note and the source items seen on the wire; the desk has not independently verified the toll, and the identities of those killed are not confirmed in the material available.

A separate ground report by News18 Hindi describes Satya Niketan as an area that began as a slum resettlement colony and grew into a hub for students, with buildings rising to as many as five storeys. The outlet attributes an account of how those upper floors came to be built to an elderly local resident; the desk has not seen the substance of that account and it should not be paraphrased further without checking the original.

The intake note says students are moving out of the area. It does not say how many, where they are going, or whether any authority has ordered them to vacate. None of that is established at this stage.

No statement from the MCD, the Delhi government, police or any building owner appears in the material seen so far. It is also not confirmed on what legal basis the 24 buildings were demolished, whether the inspected hostels face further action, or whether any arrests or FIRs have followed the collapse.

Before publication the desk needs to confirm: the death toll and any injuries with police or hospital sources; the exact date, time and address of the collapse; the MCD's own account of the inspection and demolition drive, including the notices issued and the legal grounds; whether residents or students were displaced and what relocation, if any, was offered; the status of any criminal investigation; and the details of the News18 Hindi ground report, including the resident's account, which must be independently reported rather than relied on.
